analysis.title: Editor Engagement and Talk Page Workflows Roundtable

chapters.title: Welcome Messages and Social Cues
chapters.summary: Participants discuss how new editors perceive welcome messages and debate automated greetings versus genuine social connections.

chapters.title: Personal Stories of Community Collaboration
chapters.summary: Speaker A shares experiences of early editing interactions and coordinating global cross-community collaboration on an article.

chapters.title: Wikidata's Simplified Greeting Experimentation
chapters.summary: Speaker G shares Wikidata's success with simplified welcome messages signed by recently active users to open dialogue.

chapters.title: Reversion Workflows and Talk Page Watchlists
chapters.summary: Speaker D explains the friction of tracking user talk pages during manual reversions and discovering articles passively.

chapters.title: Acknowledgments and Discovery Tools
chapters.summary: The group explores gratitude mechanisms like Barnstars, global messaging bots, and the utility of the New Pages feed before breaking into groups.

insights.text: User testing shows that recipients cannot reliably tell whether a welcome message was generated by a human or a bot, splitting opinions 50/50.
Human connection and simple greetings are significantly more effective at onboarding new editors than overwhelming them with boilerplate templates and links.
Wikidata found success sending simple automated welcome messages signed off by an editor active in the past hour to allow immediate two-way communication.
Editors who issue template warnings for reversions need notifications only when the recipient provides a substantive reply, rather than tracking all talk page activity.
Monitoring other editors' talk pages serves as a passive discovery mechanism for finding and improving articles without direct conversation.
Editor acknowledgment systems like Thanks, WikiLove, and Barnstars would benefit from counters, collections, and simple reciprocal thank-you interactions.
The New Pages feed allows experienced editors to find newly created articles, locate relevant sources, and collaborate on translations.
